file code/mc_common.py, lines 1-587\n1: \"\"\"Shared Monte Carlo utilities for Question 2 (Monte Carlo pricing & hedging).\n2: \n3: Owned by the deepseek-numerical subagent.  This module is imported by\n4: ``approach1_pricing.py``, ``approach2_hedging.py`` and ``tests/test_numerical.py``.\n5: \n6: Conventions\n7: -----------\n8: * The model is the assignment-prescribed *risk-neutral* geometric Brownian motion\n9:   with drift ``r``::\n10: \n11:       S_{t_{i+1}} = S_{t_i} * exp[(r - 0.5*sigma^2) * dt + sigma*sqrt(dt) * Z_i]\n12: \n13:   This is explicitly *not* the Black-76 (zero-drift) futures convention; it is\n14:   the model requested by the assignment for the Black-Scholes validation.\n15: * Times ``t_0=0, t_1=dt, ..., t_m=T`` with ``m = steps``.  All path-dependent\n16:   payoffs monitor ``t_1..t_m`` (the initial point ``t_0`` is *excluded*).\n17: * Discounting uses the continuous rate ``r``:  price = exp(-r T) * E[payoff].\n18: * Every stochastic component is seeded; pass an explicit ``seed``.\n19: \"\"\"\n20: \n21: from __future__ import annotations\n22: \n23: import json\n24: import math\n25: import os\n26: from dataclasses import dataclass, fields\n27: from pathlib import Path\n28: from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, Optional, Sequence, Tuple\n29: \n30: import numpy as np\n31: from scipy.stats import norm\n32: \n33: try:  # torch is optional for NumPy-only consumers (tests, quick checks)\n34:     import torch\n35: \n36:     _HAS_TORCH = True\n37: except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - torch is a hard dependency of the assignment\n38:     torch = None\n39:     _HAS_TORCH = False\n40: \n41: \n42: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n43: # Model & repository helpers\n44: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n45: \n46: @dataclass\n47: class Model:\n48:     \"\"\"Calibrated market parameters for one dataset.\n49: \n50:     Defaults follow the shared lead/subagent contract: ``K = S0`` and\n51:     ``B = 1.2 * S0``; ``T = 1`` year with ``steps = 252`` monitoring points.\n52:     \"\"\"\n53: \n54:     S0: float = 100.0\n55:     K: float = 100.0\n56:     B: float = 120.0\n57:     r: float = 0.03\n58:     sigma: float = 0.20\n59:     mu: float = 0.05\n60:     T: float = 1.0\n61:     steps: int = 252\n62: \n63:     @property\n64:     def dt(self) -> float:\n65:         return self.T / self.steps\n66: \n67:     @property\n68:     def sqrt_dt(self) -> float:\n69:         return math.sqrt(self.dt)\n70: \n71:     def asdict(self) -> Dict[str, float]:\n72:         return {f.name: getattr(self, f.name) for f in fields(self)}\n73: \n74: \n75: DEFAULT_MODEL = Model()\n76: \n77: \n78: def repo_root() -> Path:\n79:     \"\"\"Repository root (parent of the ``code`` directory).\"\"\"\n80:     return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n81: \n82: \n83: def calibration_path() -> Path:\n84:     return repo_root() / \"data\" / \"clean\" / \"calibration.json\"\n85: \n86: \n87: def load_model(path: Optional[os.PathLike] = None) -> Model:\n88:     \"\"\"Load a :class:`Model` from ``data/clean/calibration.json``.\n89: \n90:     The lead agent owns the calibration file with keys\n91:     ``S0, K, B, r, sigma, mu, T, steps``.  If the file is missing (e.g. before\n92:     data arrives) the built-in defaults are returned so the numerical modules\n93:     remain runnable.\n94:     \"\"\"\n95:     p = Path(path) if path is not None else calibration_path()\n96:     if p.exists():\n97:         data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n98:         known = {f.name for f in fields(Model)}\n99:         kwargs = {k: data[k] for k in known if k in data}\n100:         return Model(**kwargs)\n101:     return Model()\n102: \n103: \n104: def results_dir(approach: str, dataset: str) -> Path:\n105:     \"\"\"``results/<approach>/<dataset>/``, created on demand.\"\"\"\n106:     d = repo_root() / \"results\" / approach / dataset\n107:     d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n108:     return d\n109: \n110: \n111: def _to_jsonable(obj):\n112:     \"\"\"Recursively convert numpy/torch scalars & arrays to plain JSON types.\"\"\"\n113:     if obj is None or isinstance(obj, (bool, int, float, str)):\n114:         return obj\n115:     if isinstance(obj, dict):\n116:         return {k: _to_jsonable(v) for k, v in obj.items()}\n117:     if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):\n118:         return [_to_jsonable(v) for v in obj]\n119:     if hasattr(obj, \"item\"):  # numpy scalar / torch scalar\n120:         return _to_jsonable(obj.item())\n121:     if hasattr(obj, \"tolist\"):\n122:         return _to_jsonable(obj.tolist())\n123:     return str(obj)\n124: \n125: \n126: def write_metrics(path: Path, params: dict, metrics: dict, fit_seconds: float,\n127:                   history: dict) -> None:\n128:     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n129:     payload = {\n130:         \"params\": _to_jsonable(params),\n131:         \"metrics\": _to_jsonable(metrics),\n132:         \"fit_seconds\": float(fit_seconds),\n133:         \"history\": _to_jsonable(history),\n134:     }\n135:     path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n136: \n137: \n138: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n139: # Exact GBM simulation\n140: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n141: \n142: def simulate_gbm_np(model: Model, n_paths: int, seed: int,\n143:                     antithetic: bool = False) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n144:     \"\"\"Simulate GBM paths with NumPy.\n145: \n146:     Returns ``(S, Z)`` where ``S`` has shape ``(n_paths, steps + 1)`` and ``Z``\n147:     is the underlying standard-normal shock matrix ``(n_paths, steps)``.\n148: \n149:     With ``antithetic=True`` the shocks are generated as ``n_paths/2`` pairs\n150:     ``(Z, -Z)`` so the total number of simulated paths is still ``n_paths``\n151:     (equal path budget).\n152:     \"\"\"\n153:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n154:     steps = model.steps\n155:     if antithetic:\n156:         half = n_paths // 2\n157:         Z = rng.standard_normal((half, steps))\n158:         Z = np.concatenate([Z, -Z], axis=0)\n159:         Z = Z[:n_paths]\n160:     else:\n161:         Z = rng.standard_normal((n_paths, steps))\n162:     S = gbm_paths_from_z_np(model, Z)\n163:     return S, Z\n164: \n165: \n166: def gbm_paths_from_z_np(model: Model, Z: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n167:     \"\"\"Vectorized GBM path construction from a shock matrix ``Z`` (n, steps).\"\"\"\n168:     Z = np.asarray(Z, dtype=float)\n169:     drift = (model.r - 0.5 * model.sigma ** 2) * model.dt\n170:     vol = model.sigma * model.sqrt_dt\n171:     log_inc = drift + vol * Z\n172:     cum = np.concatenate([np.zeros((Z.shape[0], 1)), np.cumsum(log_inc, axis=1)], axis=1)\n173:     log_S = math.log(model.S0) + cum\n174:     return np.exp(log_S)\n175: \n176: \n177: def gbm_paths_from_z_torch(model: Model, Z: np.ndarray) -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n178:     \"\"\"GBM path construction in PyTorch from the *same* shock matrix ``Z``.\n179: \n180:     Using an identical ``Z`` (produced by the NumPy RNG) makes the two engines\n181:     agree up to floating-point precision rather than merely up to statistical\n182:     error.\n183:     \"\"\"\n184:     assert torch is not None, \"torch is required for the PyTorch engine\"\n185:     Zt = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(Z, dtype=np.float64), dtype=torch.float64)\n186:     drift = (model.r - 0.5 * model.sigma ** 2) * model.dt\n187:     vol = model.sigma * model.sqrt_dt\n188:     log_inc = drift + vol * Zt\n189:     cum = torch.cat([torch.zeros((Zt.shape[0], 1), dtype=torch.float64),\n190:                      torch.cumsum(log_inc, dim=1)], dim=1)\n191:     log_S = math.log(model.S0) + cum\n192:     return torch.exp(log_S)\n193: \n194: \n195: def simulate_gbm_loop(S0: float, r: float, sigma: float, dt: float,\n196:                       steps: int, Z: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n197:     \"\"\"Naive Python-loop GBM simulation (used only for the profiling baseline).\"\"\"\n198:     Z = np.asarray(Z, dtype=float)\n199:     n = Z.shape[0]\n200:     drift = (r - 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * dt\n201:     vol = sigma * math.sqrt(dt)\n202:     S = np.empty((n, steps + 1))\n203:     for i in range(n):\n204:         s = S0\n205:         S[i, 0] = s\n206:         row = Z[i]\n207:         for j in range(steps):\n208:             s = s * math.exp(drift + vol * row[j])\n209:             S[i, j + 1] = s\n210:     return S\n211: \n212: \n213: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n214: # Payoffs (all monitor t_1 .. t_m, excluding the initial point)\n215: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n216: \n217: def _monitored(S) -> np.ndarray:\n218:     \"\"\"Slice of S restricted to monitored times t_1..t_m.\"\"\"\n219:     return S[:, 1:] if S.ndim == 2 else S[1:]\n220: \n221: \n222: def payoff_european_call(S: np.ndarray, K: float) -> np.ndarray:\n223:     return np.maximum(S[:, -1] - K, 0.0)\n224: \n225: \n226: def payoff_asian_call(S: np.ndarray, K: float) -> np.ndarray:\n227:     return np.maximum(_monitored(S).mean(axis=1) - K, 0.0)\n228: \n229: \n230: def payoff_geometric_asian(S: np.ndarray, K: float) -> np.ndarray:\n231:     g = np.exp(np.mean(np.log(_monitored(S)), axis=1))\n232:     return np.maximum(g - K, 0.0)\n233: \n234: \n235: def payoff_up_and_out(S: np.ndarray, K: float, B: float) -> np.ndarray:\n236:     hit = _monitored(S).max(axis=1) >= B\n237:     payoff = np.maximum(S[:, -1] - K, 0.0)\n238:     return np.where(hit, 0.0, payoff)\n239: \n240: \n241: def payoff_digital(S: np.ndarray, K: float) -> np.ndarray:\n242:     return (S[:, -1] > K).astype(float)\n243: \n244: \n245: def _torch_monitored(S: \"torch.Tensor\") -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n246:     return S[:, 1:] if S.dim() == 2 else S[1:]\n247: \n248: \n249: def payoff_european_call_torch(S: \"torch.Tensor\", K: float) -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n250:     return torch.clamp(S[:, -1] - K, min=0.0)\n251: \n252: \n253: def payoff_asian_call_torch(S: \"torch.Tensor\", K: float) -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n254:     return torch.clamp(_torch_monitored(S).mean(dim=1) - K, min=0.0)\n255: \n256: \n257: def payoff_geometric_asian_torch(S: \"torch.Tensor\", K: float) -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n258:     g = torch.exp(torch.mean(torch.log(_torch_monitored(S)), dim=1))\n259:     return torch.clamp(g - K, min=0.0)\n260: \n261: \n262: def payoff_up_and_out_torch(S: \"torch.Tensor\", K: float, B: float) -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n263:     hit = _torch_monitored(S).max(dim=1).values >= B\n264:     payoff = torch.clamp(S[:, -1] - K, min=0.0)\n265:     return torch.where(hit, torch.zeros_like(payoff), payoff)\n266: \n267: \n268: def payoff_digital_torch(S: \"torch.Tensor\", K: float) -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n269:     return (S[:, -1] > K).to(torch.float64)\n270: \n271: \n272: PAYOFFS = {\n273:     \"european\": payoff_european_call,\n274:     \"asian\": payoff_asian_call,\n275:     \"barrier\": payoff_up_and_out,\n276:     \"digital\": payoff_digital,\n277: }\n278: \n279: PAYOFFS_TORCH = {\n280:     \"european\": payoff_european_call_torch,\n281:     \"asian\": payoff_asian_call_torch,\n282:     \"barrier\": payoff_up_and_out_torch,\n283:     \"digital\": payoff_digital_torch,\n284: }\n285: \n286: \n287: def mc_price_np(model: Model, n_paths: int, seed: int,\n288:                 antithetic: bool = False) -> Dict[str, dict]:\n289:     \"\"\"Price all four payoffs with the NumPy engine.\n290: \n291:     Returns a dict ``name -> {\"price\", \"se\", \"n\"}``.  ``antithetic`` prices use\n292:     the same total path budget as the naive run (``n_paths`` paths).\n293:     \"\"\"\n294:     S, _ = simulate_gbm_np(model, n_paths, seed, antithetic=antithetic)\n295:     disc = math.exp(-model.r * model.T)\n296:     out: Dict[str, dict] = {}\n297:     n_eff = S.shape[0] if not antithetic else S.shape[0] // 2\n298:     for name, fn in PAYOFFS.items():\n299:         if name == \"barrier\":\n300:             vals = fn(S, model.K, model.B)\n301:         else:\n302:             vals = fn(S, model.K)\n303:         if antithetic:\n304:             vals = (vals[:n_eff] + vals[n_eff:2 * n_eff]) / 2.0\n305:         out[name] = {\n306:             \"price\": float(disc * vals.mean()),\n307:             \"se\": float(disc * vals.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(vals.shape[0])),\n308:             \"n\": int(vals.shape[0]),\n309:         }\n310:     return out\n311: \n312: \n313: def mc_price_torch(model: Model, n_paths: int, seed: int,\n314:                    antithetic: bool = False) -> Dict[str, dict]:\n315:     \"\"\"Price all four payoffs with the PyTorch engine (identical shocks).\"\"\"\n316:     _, Z = simulate_gbm_np(model, n_paths, seed, antithetic=antithetic)\n317:     S = gbm_paths_from_z_torch(model, Z)\n318:     disc = math.exp(-model.r * model.T)\n319:     out: Dict[str, dict] = {}\n320:     n_eff = S.shape[0] if not antithetic else S.shape[0] // 2\n321:     for name, fn in PAYOFFS_TORCH.items():\n322:         if name == \"barrier\":\n323:             vals = fn(S, model.K, model.B)\n324:         else:\n325:             vals = fn(S, model.K)\n326:         if antithetic:\n327:             vals = (vals[:n_eff] + vals[n_eff:2 * n_eff]) / 2.0\n328:         arr = vals.detach().numpy()\n329:         out[name] = {\n330:             \"price\": float(disc * arr.mean()),\n331:             \"se\": float(disc * arr.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(arr.shape[0])),\n332:             \"n\": int(arr.shape[0]),\n333:         }\n334:     return out\n335: \n336: \n337: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n338: # Black-Scholes references (European vanilla call)\n339: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n340: \n341: def _d1_d2(S0: float, K: float, r: float, sigma: float, T: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:\n342:     if T <= 0 or sigma <= 0:\n343:         return (0.0, 0.0)\n344:     d1 = (math.log(S0 / K) + (r + 0.5 * sigma ** 2) * T) / (sigma * math.sqrt(T))\n345:     d2 = d1 - sigma * math.sqrt(T)\n346:     return d1, d2\n347: \n348: \n349: def bs_call_price(S0: float, K: float, r: float, sigma: float, T: float) -> float:\n350:     d1, d2 = _d1_d2(S0, K, r, sigma, T)\n351:     return S0 * norm.cdf(d1) - K * math.exp(-r * T) * norm.cdf(d2)\n352: \n353: \n354: def bs_call_delta(S0: float, K: float, r: float, sigma: float, T: float) -> float:\n355:     d1, _ = _d1_d2(S0, K, r, sigma, T)\n356:     return float(norm.cdf(d1))\n357: \n358: \n359: def bs_call_vega(S0: float, K: float, r: float, sigma: float, T: float) -> float:\n360:     d1, _ = _d1_d2(S0, K, r, sigma, T)\n361:     return float(S0 * math.sqrt(T) * norm.pdf(d1))\n362: \n363: \n364: def bs_call_delta_at(S_t: float, K: float, r: float, sigma: float, tau: float) -> float:\n365:     \"\"\"Black-Scholes delta of a vanilla call with time-to-maturity ``tau``.\"\"\"\n366:     if tau <= 0:\n367:         return float(S_t > K)\n368:     d1 = (math.log(S_t / K) + (r + 0.5 * sigma ** 2) * tau) / (sigma * math.sqrt(tau))\n369:     return float(norm.cdf(d1))\n370: \n371: \n372: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n373: # Discrete geometric-Asian closed form\n374: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n375: \n376: def geometric_asian_price(S0: float, K: float, r: float, sigma: float,\n377:                           T: float, steps: int) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:\n378:     \"\"\"Discounted price of a geometric-Asian call for the *discrete* schedule\n379:     ``t_1..t_m`` (m = steps, equally spaced, initial point excluded).\n380: \n381:     Returns ``(price, mu_G, var_G)`` where ``mu_G = E[ln G]`` and\n382:     ``var_G = Var[ln G]``.\n383:     \"\"\"\n384:     m = steps\n385:     mu_G = math.log(S0) + (r - 0.5 * sigma ** 2) * T * (m + 1) / (2 * m)\n386:     var_G = sigma ** 2 * T * (m + 1) * (2 * m + 1) / (6 * m * m)\n387:     s_G = math.sqrt(var_G)\n388:     E_G = math.exp(mu_G + 0.5 * var_G)\n389:     d1 = (mu_G + var_G - math.log(K)) / s_G\n390:     d2 = d1 - s_G\n391:     price = math.exp(-r * T) * (E_G * norm.cdf(d1) - K * norm.cdf(d2))\n392:     return float(price), float(mu_G), float(var_G)\n393: \n394: \n395: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n396: # Statistical helpers\n397: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n398: \n399: def se_of(x: np.ndarray) -> float:\n400:     x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)\n401:     if x.shape[0] < 2:\n402:         return float(\"nan\")\n403:     return float(x.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(x.shape[0]))\n404: \n405: \n406: def variance_reduction_ratio(naive: np.ndarray, reduced: np.ndarray,\n407:                              n_boot: int = 2000, seed: int = 0,\n408:                              paired: bool = True, scale: float = 1.0) -> dict:\n409:     \"\"\"Variance-reduction ratio ``Var(naive) / (scale * Var(reduced))`` with a\n410:     bootstrap CI.\n411: \n412:     ``scale`` accounts for estimators that consume a different path budget.  For\n413:     a control variate, ``naive`` and ``reduced`` use the same N paths and are\n414:     aligned per-path (``paired=True``, ``scale=1``).  For antithetic sampling\n415:     each reduced value is an average of a ``(Z, -Z)`` pair that consumes two\n416:     paths, so the equal-path-budget ratio uses ``scale=2`` and the bootstrap\n417:     resamples the two arrays independently (``paired=False``).\n418:     \"\"\"\n419:     naive = np.asarray(naive, dtype=float)\n420:     reduced = np.asarray(reduced, dtype=float)\n421:     vn = naive.var(ddof=1)\n422:     vr = reduced.var(ddof=1)\n423:     ratio = vn / (scale * vr) if vr > 0 else float(\"nan\")\n424:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n425:     boots = np.empty(n_boot)\n426:     for b in range(n_boot):\n427:         if paired:\n428:             ii = rng.integers(0, naive.shape[0], size=naive.shape[0])\n429:             vnb = naive[ii].var(ddof=1)\n430:             vrb = reduced[ii].var(ddof=1)\n431:         else:\n432:             vnb = naive[rng.integers(0, naive.shape[0], naive.shape[0])].var(ddof=1)\n433:             vrb = reduced[rng.integers(0, reduced.shape[0], reduced.shape[0])].var(ddof=1)\n434:         boots[b] = vnb / (scale * vrb) if vrb > 0 else float(\"nan\")\n435:     lo, hi = np.nanpercentile(boots, [2.5, 97.5])\n436:     return {\n437:         \"ratio\": float(ratio),\n438:         \"naive_var\": float(vn),\n439:         \"reduced_var\": float(vr),\n440:         \"scale\": float(scale),\n441:         \"ci_low\": float(lo),\n442:         \"ci_high\": float(hi),\n443:         \"n_boot\": n_boot,\n444:     }\n445: \n446: \n447: def paired_bootstrap_se(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray, n_boot: int = 2000,\n448:                         seed: int = 0) -> Tuple[float, float]:\n449:     \"\"\"Paired-bootstrap standard error of ``mean(a) - mean(b)``.\n450: \n451:     ``a`` and ``b`` are aligned per-path contributions.\n452:     \"\"\"\n453:     a = np.asarray(a, dtype=float)\n454:     b = np.asarray(b, dtype=float)\n455:     diff = a - b\n456:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n457:     n = a.shape[0]\n458:     boots = np.empty(n_boot)\n459:     for k in range(n_boot):\n460:         ii = rng.integers(0, n, size=n)\n461:         boots[k] = diff[ii].mean()\n462:     return float(diff.mean()), float(boots.std(ddof=1))\n463: \n464: \n465: def mc_rmse_slope(ns: Sequence[int], rmse: np.ndarray) -> dict:\n466:     \"\"\"OLS slope of ``log10(rmse)`` vs ``log10(n)`` plus its standard error.\"\"\"\n467:     x = np.log10(np.asarray(ns, dtype=float))\n468:     y = np.log10(np.asarray(rmse, dtype=float))\n469:     A = np.vstack([np.ones_like(x), x]).T\n470:     (intercept, slope), *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, y, rcond=None)\n471:     resid = y - A @ np.array([intercept, slope])\n472:     dof = x.shape[0] - 2\n473:     s2 = float(resid @ resid) / dof if dof > 0 else float(\"nan\")\n474:     cov = s2 * np.linalg.inv(A.T @ A)\n475:     return {\n476:         \"slope\": float(slope),\n477:         \"slope_se\": float(math.sqrt(cov[1, 1])),\n478:         \"intercept\": float(intercept),\n479:     }\n480: \n481: \n482: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n483: # Pathwise Greeks\n484: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n485: \n486: def pathwise_vanilla_delta(model: Model, S: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n487:     disc = math.exp(-model.r * model.T)\n488:     ind = (S[:, -1] > model.K).astype(float)\n489:     return disc * ind * (S[:, -1] / model.S0)\n490: \n491: \n492: def pathwise_vanilla_vega(model: Model, S: np.ndarray, W_T: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n493:     disc = math.exp(-model.r * model.T)\n494:     ind = (S[:, -1] > model.K).astype(float)\n495:     return disc * ind * S[:, -1] * (W_T - model.sigma * model.T)\n496: \n497: \n498: def brownian_paths_from_z(model: Model, Z: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n499:     \"\"\"W(t_i) for i=0..steps from the shock matrix ``Z`` (W_0 = 0).\"\"\"\n500:     inc = model.sqrt_dt * Z\n501:     return np.concatenate([np.zeros((Z.shape[0], 1)), np.cumsum(inc, axis=1)], axis=1)\n502: \n503: \n504: def pathwise_asian_delta(model: Model, S: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n505:     disc = math.exp(-model.r * model.T)\n506:     mean_S = _monitored(S).mean(axis=1)\n507:     ind = (mean_S > model.K).astype(float)\n508:     return disc * ind * (mean_S / model.S0)\n509: \n510: \n511: def pathwise_asian_vega(model: Model, S: np.ndarray, W: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n512:     disc = math.exp(-model.r * model.T)\n513:     t = model.dt * np.arange(1, model.steps + 1)  # monitored times t_1..t_m\n514:     Sm = _monitored(S)                       # (n, m)\n515:     Wm = W[:, 1:]                             # (n, m)\n516:     dS_dsigma = Sm * (Wm - model.sigma * t)   # (n, m)\n517:     mean_deriv = dS_dsigma.mean(axis=1)\n518:     ind = (Sm.mean(axis=1) > model.K).astype(float)\n519:     return disc * ind * mean_deriv\n520: \n521: \n522: def finite_difference_greek(model: Model, n_paths: int, seed: int, payoff: Callable,\n523:                             param: str, h: float) -> dict:\n524:     \"\"\"Central finite-difference Greek with common random numbers.\n525: \n526:     ``param`` is ``\"S0\"`` (delta) or ``\"sigma\"`` (vega); ``h`` is the fractional\n527:     bump (bump = ``h * S0`` or ``h * sigma``).\n528:     \"\"\"\n529:     Z = np.random.default_rng(seed).standard_normal((n_paths, model.steps))\n530:     up = Model(**{**model.asdict(), param: getattr(model, param) * (1 + h)})\n531:     dn = Model(**{**model.asdict(), param: getattr(model, param) * (1 - h)})\n532:     S_up = gbm_paths_from_z_np(up, Z)\n533:     S_dn = gbm_paths_from_z_np(dn, Z)\n534:     disc_up = math.exp(-up.r * up.T)\n535:     disc_dn = math.exp(-dn.r * dn.T)\n536:     p_up = disc_up * payoff(S_up, up.K) if param == \"S0\" else disc_up * payoff(S_up, up.K)\n537:     p_dn = disc_dn * payoff(S_dn, dn.K)\n538:     scale = getattr(model, param)\n539:     contrib = (p_up - Greek helpers\n47: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n48: \n49: DELTA_BUMPS = [0.1, 0.01, 0.001]\n50: \n51: \n52: def _payoff_fn(name: str) -> Callable:\n53:     def fn(S, model):\n54:         if name == \"barrier\":\n55:             return PAYOFFS[name](S, model.K, model.B)\n56:         return PAYOFFS[name](S, model.K)\n57:     return fn\n58: \n59: \n60: def compute_fd_greeks(model: Model, n_paths: int, seed: int,\n61:                       name: str) -> Dict[str, dict]:\n62:     \"\"\"Central finite-difference delta & vega for one payoff with CRN.\n63: \n64:     Delta bumps use ``h * S0``; vega bumps use ``h * sigma``.  The same shock\n65:     matrix ``Z`` drives the up/down legs (common random numbers).  For delta the\n66:     up/down legs are obtained by scaling the base path (exact for a GBM whose\n67:     only S0 dependence is a multiplicative factor); vega re-simulates with the\n68:     same ``Z``.\n69:     \"\"\"\n70:     payoff = _payoff_fn(name)\n71:     disc = math.exp(-model.r * model.T)\n72:     Z = np.random.default_rng(seed).standard_normal((n_paths, model.steps))\n73:     S_base    contrib = disc * (payoff(S_up, model) - payoff(S_dn, model)) / (2 * h * model.S0)\n80:         out[\"delta\"][str(h)] = {\n81:             \"estimate\": float(contrib.mean()), \"se\": mc.se_of(contrib), \"h\": h,\n82:         }\n83:     for h in DELTA_BUMPS:\n84:         up = Model(**{**model.asdict(), \"sigma\": model.sigma * (1 + h)})\n85:         dn = Model(**{**model.asdict(), \"sigma\": model.sigma * (1 - h)})\n86:         S_up = mc.gbm_paths_from_z_np(up, Z)\n87:         S_dn = mc.gbm_paths_from_z_np(dn, Z)\n88:         contrib = (math.exp(-up.r * up.T) * payoff(S_up, mc.se_of(contrib), \"h\": h,\n92:         }\n93:     return out\n94: \n95: \n96: def _pathwise_estimators(model: Model, n_paths: int, seed: int) -> Dict[str, dict]:\n97:     \"\"\"Pathwise delta & float) -> Dict[str, dict]:\n122:     \"\"\"Naive / antithetic / control-variate estimates of the Asian call.\n123: \n124:     ``beta`` is the control coefficient from an independent pilot sample.\n125:     ``geo_price`` is the closed-form discounted geometric-Asian price.\n126:     \"\"\"\n127:     disc = math.exp(-model.r * model.T)\n128:     E_G_undisc = math.exp(model.r * model.T) * mc.payoff_geometric_asian(S_naive, model.K)\n133:     cv = A_naive - beta * (G_naive - E_G_undisc)\n134: \n135:     S_anti, _ = simulate_gbm_np(model, n_paths, seed + 1, antithetic=True)\n136: ses[\"asian_naive\"].append(disc * A.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(n))\n198:             G = mc.payoff_geometric_asian(S, model.K)\n199:             cv = disc * (A - beta * (G - E_G_undisc))\n200:             err[\"asian_cv\"].append((cv.mean() - ref_price) ** 2)\n201:             ses[\"asian_cv\"].append(mc.se_of(cv))\n202: \n203:             S_a, _ = simulate_gbm_np(model, n, s + 1, antithetic=True)\n204:             A_a = mc.payoff_asian_call(S_a, model.K)\n205:             half = n // 2\n206:             pair = disc * (A_a[:half] + A_a[half:2 * half]) / 2.0\n207:             err[\"asian_anti\"].append((pair.mean() - ref_price) ** 2)\n208:             ses[\"asian_anti\"].append(mc.se_of(pair))\n209: \n210:         for k in keys:\n211:             rmse[k].append(float(math.sqrt(float(np.mean(err[k])))))\n212:             se_mean[k].append(float(np.mean(ses[k])))\n213: \n214:     out = {\n215:         \"ns\": [int(n) for n in ns],\n216:         \"repeats\": repeats,\n217:         \"reference_price\": float(ref_price),\n218:         \"reference_source\": \"independent large antithetic MC (arithmetic Asian) \"\n219:                              \"and closed-form BS (vanilla)\",\n220:         \"rmse\": rmse,\n221:         \"se_mean\": se_mean,\n222:     }\n223:     for k in keys:\n224:         out[f\"slope_rmse_{k}\"] = mc_rmse_slope(ns, np.asarray(rmse[k]))\n225:         out[f\"slope_se_{k}\"] = mc_rmse_slope(ns, np.asarray(se_mean[k]))\n226:     return out\n227: \n228: \n229: # Linear pipeline:\n4: \n5:     load model -> simulate train/val/test paths -> train CVaR-optimal MLP policy\n6:     (per transaction-cost level) -> evaluate against Black-Scholes delta hedging\n7:     (frequencies 1/5/21, costs 0/10/50 bp) and a zero-hedge baseline\n8:     -> paired bootstrap CIs -> write outputs\n9: \n10: Usage (from the repository root)::\n11: \n12:     uv run python code/approach2_hedging.py --seed 42 --dataset if_main\n13: \n14: Conventions (identical across neural and baseline policies)\n15: ----------------------------------------------------------\n16: * We are short one European call ``H(S) = max(S_T - K, 0)`` and hedge with the\n17:   underlying.  The terminal hedging P&L is the assignment-specified::\n18: \n19:       V_T = sum_t exp(r (T - t)) * Delta_t * (S_{t+dt} - S_t)\n20:             - kappa * sum_t |Delta_t - Delta_{t-1}| * S_t - H(S)\n21: \n22: * Initial holding is zero (``Delta_{-1} = 0``), no premium is received, costs are\n23:   *not* interest-accumulated, and there is *no* terminal closeout (the final\n24:   position is not unwound).  Rebalancing happens on a fixed grid of ``freq``\n25:   days; the position chosen at the last rebalancing time is held to maturity.\n26: * Loss ``L = -V_T``; we minimize the 95% CVaR of ``L`` with the\n27:   Rockafellar-Uryasev objective ``eta + mean(relu(L - eta)) / (1 - alpha)``.\n28: \"\"\"\n29: \n30: from __future__ import annotations\n31: \n32: import argparse\n33: import math\n34: import \n53: from rich.console import Console  # noqa: E402\n54: from rich.panel import Panel  # noqa: E402\n55: from rich.table import Table  # noqa: E402\n56: \n57: console = Console()\n58: \n59: FREQS = formula)\n66: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n67: \n68: def rebal_indices(steps: int, freq: int) -> np.ndarray:\n69:     \"\"\"Rebalancing step indices ``0, freq, 2*freq, ... < steps``.\"\"\"\n70:     return np.arange(0, steps, freq)\n71: \n72: \n73: def hedging_pnl_np(S: np.ndarray, delta: np.ndarray, rebal_idx: np.ndarray,\n74:                    kappa: float, model: Model) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n75:     \"\"\"Terminal hedging P&L (NumPy, vectorized).\n76: \n77:     Returns ``(V, turnover, total_cost)`` of shape ``(B,)``.\n78:     \"\"\"\n79:     idx = np.asarray(rebal_idx, dtype=int)\n80:     next_idx = np.empty_like(idx)\n81:     next_idx[:-1] = idx[1:]\n82:     next_idx[-1] = model.steps\n83:     S_tau = S[:, idx]           # (B, n_rebal)\n84:     S_next = S[:, next_idx]     # (B, n_rebal)\n85:     t = idx * model.dt\n86:     w = np.exp(model.r * (model.T - t))[None, :]  # (1, n_rebal)\n87:     gains = (w * delta * (S_next - S_tau)).sum(axis=1)\n88: \n89:     prev = np.concatenate([np.zeros((S.shape[0], 1)), delta[:, :-1]], axis=1)\n90:     trade = delta - prev\n91:     turnover = np.abs(trade).sum(axis=1)\n92:     costs = kappa * (np.abs(trade) * S_tau).sum(axis=1)\n93: \n94:     H = np.maximum(S[:, -1] - model.K, 0.0)\n95:     V = gains - costs - H\n96:     return V, turnover, costs\n97: \n98: \n99: def hedging_pnl_torch(S: \"torch.Tensor\", delta: \"torch.Tensor\",\n100:                       rebal_idx: np.ndarray, kappa: float,\n101:                       model: Model) -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n102:     \"\"\"Terminal hedging P&L (PyTorch, vectorized & differentiable in ``delta``).\n103: \n104:     Returns ``V`` of shape ``(B,)`` (loss ``L = -V`` is minimized).\n105:     \"\"\"\n106:     idx = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(rebal_idx, dtype=int), dtype=torch.long,\n107:                           device=S.device)\n108:     n = idx.shape[0]\n109:     next_idx = torch.empty(n, dtype=torch.long, device=S.device)\n110:     next_idx[:-1] = idx[1:]\n111:     next_idx[-1] = model.steps\n112:     S_tau = S[:, idx]           # (B, n)\n113:     S_next = S[:, next_idx]     # (B, n)\n114:     t = idx.float() * model.dt\n115:     w = torch.exp(model.r * (model.T - t)).unsqueeze(0)  # (1, n)\n116:     gains = (w * delta * (S_next - S_tau)).sum(dim=1)\n117: \n118:     prev = torch.cat([torch.zeros(S.shape[0], 1, dtype=S.dtype, device=S.device),\n119:                       delta[:, :-1]], dim=1)\n120:     trade = delta - prev\n121:     costs = kappa * (trade.abs() * S_tau).sum(dim=1)\n122: \n123:     H = torch.clamp(S[:, -1] - model.K, min=0.0)\n124:     return gains - costs - H\n125: \n126: \n127: def bs_delta_schedule(S: np.ndarray, rebal_idx: np.ndarray, model: Model) -> np.ndarray:\n128:     \"\"\"Black-Scholes delta at each rebalancing time.\"\"\"\n129:     S_tau = S[:, rebal_idx]\n130:     tau = rebal_idx * model.dt\n131:     remaining = model.T - tau\n132:     d1 = (np.log(S_tau / model.K) + (model.r + 0.5 * model.sigma ** 2) * remaining) \\\n133:         / (model.sigma * np.sqrt(remaining))\n134:     return norm.cdf(d1)\n135: \n136: \n137: def empirical_cvar(losses: np.ndarray, alpha: float = ALPHA) -> Tuple[float, float]:\n138:     \"\"\"Fractional empirical VaR and CVaR of the *upper* tail of ``losses``.\"\"\"\n139:     x = np.sort(np.asarray(losses, dtype=float))\n140:     n = x.shape[0]\n141:     k = int(math.ceil(alpha * n))\n142:     var_ = x[k - 1]\n143:     cvar = ((k - alpha * n) * x[k - 1] + x[k:].sum()) / (n * (1.0 - alpha))\n144:     return float(var_), float(cvar)\n145: \n146: \n147: def loss_metrics(losses: np.ndarray) -> dict:\n148:     \"\"\"VaR/CVaR (upper tail), variance and expectation of ``-V`` losses.\"\"\"\n149:     var_, cvar = empirical_cvar(losses)\n150:     return {\n151:         \"cvar95\": cvar,\n152:         \"var95\": var_,\n153:         \"pnl_variance\": float(losses.var(ddof=1)),\n154:         \"expected_pnl\": float(-losses.mean()),  # E[V_T] = -E[L]\n155:         \"expected_loss\": float(losses.mean()),\n156:     }\n157: \n158: \n159: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n160: # Neural policy\n161: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n162: \n163: class PolicyMLP(nn.Module):\n164:     \"\"\"Delta_t = f_theta(S_t / S_0, t/T) with two hidden layers (<= 32 units).\"\"\"\n165: \n166:     def __init__(self, hidden: int = 32, init_delta: float = 0.5):\n167:         super().__init__()\n168:         self.net = nn.Sequential(\n169:             nn.Linear(2, hidden), nn.SiLU(),\n170:             nn.Linear(hidden, hidden), nn.SiLU(),\n171:             nn.Linear(hidden, 1),\n172:         )\n173:         with torch.no_grad():\n174:             self.net[-1].bias.fill_(init_delta)\n175:             self.net[-1].weight.fill_(0.0)\n176: \n177:     def forward(self, x: \"torch.Tensor\") -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n178:         # x: (..., 2) -> (...,)\n179:         return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)\n180: \n181: \n182: def _policy_inputs(S: \"torch.Tensor\", model: Model, rebal_idx: np.ndarray) -> \"torch.Tensor\":\n183:     \"\"\"(B, n_rebal, 2) features ``[S_t/S0, t/T]``.\"\"\"\n184:     t = torch.as_tensor(rebal_idx * model.dt / model.T, dtype=S.dtype, device=S.device)\n185:     x1 = S[:, rebal_idx] / model.S0\n186:     x2 = t.unsqueeze(0).expand(x1.shape[0], -1)\n187:     return torch.stack([x1, x2], dim=-1)\n188: \n189: \n190: def neural_delta(policy: PolicyMLP, S: \"torch.Tensor\", model: Model,\n191: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n196: # Data generation\n197: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n198: \n199: def simulate_dataset(model: Model, n_paths: int, seed: int,\n200:                      dtype: np.dtype = np.float32) -> np.ndarray:\n201:     \"\"\"Simulate ``(n_paths, steps+1)`` GBM paths with a chunked NumPy RNG.\"\"\"\n202:     S = np.empty((n_paths, model.steps + 1), dtype=dtype)\n203:     rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n204:     chunk = 1 << 15\n205:     done = 0\n206:     while done < n_paths:\n207:         c = min(chunk, n_paths - done)\n208:         Z = rng.standard_normal((c, model.steps))\n209:         Sc = gbm_paths_from_z_np(model, Z)\n210:         S[done:done + c] = Sc.astype(dtype)\n211:         done += c\n212:     return S\n213: \n214: \n215: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n216: # Training\n217: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n218: \n219: def train_policy(model: Model, S_train: \"torch.Tensor\", S_val: \"torch.Tensor\",\n220:                  kappa: float, seed: int, args) -> dict:\n221:     torch.manual_seed(seed)\n222:     policy = PolicyMLP(args.hidden, init_delta=bs_call_delta(\n223:         model.S0, model.K, model.r, model.sigma, model.T))\n224:     rebal_idx = rebal_indices(model.steps, 1)  # daily training grid\n225: \n226:     # Initialise the quantile level eta at the empirical 95%-VaR of the initial\n227:     # S_init = S_train[:min(S_train.shape[0], 8192)]\n231:         d_init = neural_delta(policy, S_init, model, rebal_idx)\n232:         V_init = hedging_pnl_torch(S_init, d_init, rebal_idx, kappa, model)\n233:         init_eta = float(np.quantile((-V_init).numpy(), ALPHA))\n234:     eta = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(init_eta, dtype=torch.float32))\n235:     # separate optimizers: the quantile level eta needs a much larger learning\n236:     # rate than the network weights to track the (unknown) VaR level.\n237:     optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(policy.parameters(), lr=args.lr)\n238:     optimizer_eta = torch.optim.Adam([eta], lr=args.lr_eta)\n239: \n240:     n_train = S_train.shape[0]\n241:     n_batch = args.batch_size\n242:     alpha = ALPHA\n243:     inv_tail = 1.0 / (1.0 - alpha)\n244: \n245:     best_val = float(\"inf\")\n246:     best_state = None\n247:     patience_left = args.patience\n248:     history = {\"train_loss\": [], \"val_cvar\": [], \"val_var\": [], \"eta\": [],\n249:                \"grad_norm\": []}\n250: \n251:     for epoch in range(args.epochs):\n252:         policy.train()\n253:         perm = torch.randperm(n_train)\n254:         epoch_loss = 0.0\n255:         n_steps = 0\n256:         for i in range(0, n_train, n_batch):\n257:             idx = perm[i:i + n_batch]\n258:             S = S_train[idx]\n259:             delta = Begin Patch\n*** Add File: tools/report_results.py\n+\"\"\"Render factual report tables directly from executed, full-size metrics.\"\"\"\n+import argparse\n+import json\n+from pathlib import Path\n+\n+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n+\n+\n+def table(headers, rows):\n+    render = lambda row: \"| \" + \" | \".join(f\"{x:.8g}\" if isinstance(x,float) else str(x) for x in row) + \" |\"\n+    return \"\\n\".join([render(headers),render([\"---\"]*len(headers)),*[render(row) for row in rows]])\n+\n+\n+def main():\n+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n+    parser.add_argument(\"--hedging-dataset\",default=\"if_main\")\n+    args = parser.parse_args()\n+    ap = \"results/approach1/if_main/metrics.json\"\n+    bp = f\"results/approach2/{args.hedging_dataset}/metrics.json\"\n+    a,b = [json.loads((ROOT/path).read_text()) for path in (ap,bp)]\n+    if b[\"params\"][\"n_train\"] < 2**17:\n+        raise ValueError(\"Cannot report smoke run as full training\")\n+    am,bm = a[\"metrics\"],b[\"metrics\"]\n+    lines = [\"<!-- GENERATED_RESULTS_START -->\",f\"The following tables are generated from `{ap}` and `{bp}`. Values are index-point payoffs/P&L; the digital pays one unit.\",\n+             \"### Executed pricing and validation\"]\n+    lines.append(table([\"Payoff\",\"NumPy price\",\"SE\",\"95% lower\",\"95% upper\",\"PyTorch price\"],[\n+        [name,v[\"price\"],v[\"se\"],v[\"price\"]-1.96*v[\"se\"],v[\"price\"]+1.96*v[\"se\"],am[\"prices\"][\"torch\"][name][\"price\"]]\n+        for name,v in am[\"prices\"][\"numpy\"].items()]))\n+    val = am[\"validation\"]\n+    lines.append(f\"European BS reference: {val['european_bs']:.10f}; MC z-score: {val['z_score']:.6f}; criterion passed: {val['z_pass']}. Engines use identical shocks; their agreement checks arithmetic implementation, not independence of RNG libraries.\")\n+    vr = am[\"variance_reduction\"]\n+    lines += [\"### Asian variance reduction\",table([\"Estimator\",\"Price\",\"SE\",\"Variance of estimate\",\"95% lower\",\"95% upper\"],[\n+        [name,v[\"price\"],v[\"se\"],v[\"se\"]**2,v[\"price\"]-1.96*v[\"se\"],v[\"price\"]+1.96*v[\"se\"]] for name,v in vr[\"asian\"].items()]),\n+        f\"Independent-pilot coefficient beta: {vr['beta']:.9f}. Production path budgets are matched; pilot overhead is additional.\",\n+        table([\"Method\",\"Variance reduction\",\"Bootstrap lower\",\"Bootstrap upper\"],[[name,vr[key][\"ratio\"],vr[key][\"ci_low\"],vr[key][\"ci_high\"]] for name,key in [(\"Antithetic\",\"vrr_antithetic\"),(\"Control variate\",\"vrr_cv\")]])]\n+    g = am[\"greeks\"]\n+    rows = []\n+    for payoff,quantities in g[\"fd\"].items():\n+        for quantity,bumps in quantities.items():\n+            pw = g[\"pathwise\"].get(\"vanilla\" if payoff==\"european\" else payoff,{}).get(quantity,{})\n+            for bump,v in bumps.items():\n+                rows.append([payoff,quantity,bump,v[\"estimate\"],v[\"se\"],pw.get(\"estimate\",\"invalid pathwise\"),pw.get(\"se\",\"—\")])\n+    lines += [\"### Greeks\",table([\"Payoff\",\"Greek\",\"Fractional bump\",\"FD\",\"FD SE\",\"Pathwise\",\"Pathwise SE\"],rows),\n+              \"Large spot bumps introduce smoothing/truncation bias. Discontinuous payoffs can have rising finite-difference variance as bumps shrink; a sample SE is not an estimate of truncation bias.\",\n+              \"### Convergence\",table([\"Estimator\",\"RMSE slope\",\"OLS slope SE\",\"SE-versus-N slope\"],[\n+                  [key,am[\"convergence\"][f\"slope_rmse_{key}\"][\"slope\"],am[\"convergence\"][f\"slope_rmse_{key}\"][\"slope_se\"],am[\"convergence\"][f\"slope_se_{key}\"][\"slope\"]]\n+                  for key in (\"vanilla_naive\",\"asian_naive\",\"asian_anti\",\"asian_cv\")]),\n+              f\"Independent Asian reference: `{json.dumps(a['history']['ref'],sort_keys=True)}`. All reference uncertainty and observed departures are retained in the metrics.\"]\n+    pr = am[\"profiling\"]\n+    lines += [\"### Profiling\",table([\"Loop seconds\",\"NumPy seconds\",\"Speedup\",\"Loop peak bytes\",\"NumPy peak bytes\"],[[pr[k] for k in (\"naive_loop_seconds\",\"vectorized_seconds\",\"speedup\",\"naive_loop_peak_memory_bytes\",\"vectorized_peak_memory_bytes\")]]),\n+              \"These are matched supplied-shock workloads. Memory values are traced allocations, not total process RSS. The raw hot-loop profile is stored in the metrics history. CPU contention can affect wall-clock measurements.\",\n+              \"### Full-size neural training\",\n+              f\"Architecture: {b['params']['architecture']}, SiLU hidden activations, unconstrained scalar output. Training paths: {b['params']['n_train']}; validation: {b['params']['n_val']}; test: {b['params']['n_test']}. Seeds: `{json.dumps(b['params']['seeds'])}`. Adam learning rates: weights {b['params']['lr']}, eta {b['params']['lr_eta']}; batch size {b['params']['batch_size']}; maximum epochs {b['params']['epochs']}; validation patience {b['params']['patience']}; CPU threads {b['params']['threads']}.\",\n+              table([\"Training cost\",\"Epochs\",\"Best validation CVaR\",\"Restored eta\"],[[k,v[\"epochs_run\"],v[\"best_val_cvar\"],v[\"best_eta\"]] for k,v in bm[\"training\"].items()]),\n+              \"Policies train on the daily grid. The 5/21-day results evaluate those same policies at fewer decision times; they are not separately optimized frequency-specific networks. Restored models minimize validation CVaR among observed epochs; convergence to the global CVaR optimum is not established.\",\n+              \"### All held-out frequency/cost benchmarks\"]\n+    rows=[]\n+    for freq in (1,5,21):\n+        for cost in (0.,.001,.005):\n+            for policy,v in [(\"BS\",bm[\"bs\"][str(freq)][str(cost)]),(\"Neural\",bm[\"neural\"][str(cost)][str(freq)][str(cost)]),(\"Zero\",bm[\"zero_hedge\"])]:\n+                rows.append([freq,cost,policy,*[v[k] for k in (\"cvar95\",\"expected_pnl\",\"pnl_variance\",\"avg_cost\",\"turnover\")]])\n+    lines += [table([\"Days\",\"Cost\",\"Policy\",\"CVaR95\",\"Mean P&L\",\"P&L variance\",\"Mean cost\",\"Turnover (units)\"],rows),\n+              \"### Paired bootstrap uncertainty\",table([\"Combination\",\"Observed neural minus BS CVaR\",\"95% lower\",\"95% upper\"],[[k,v.get(\"point_diff\",v[\"mean_diff\"]),v[\"ci_low\"],v[\"ci_high\"]] for k,v in bm[\"bootstrap_cis_neural_minus_bs\"].items()]),\n+              \"Negative differences favor neural hedging; intervals crossing zero are inconclusive. These are marginal paired-path bootstrap intervals conditional on each fitted model, without multiplicity adjustment or independent retraining. No general outperformance claim follows from this single training seed.\",\n+              f\"Recorded approach wall times: A {a['fit_seconds']:.3f}s, B {b['fit_seconds']:.3f}s. Source figures: `results/approach1/if_main/{{convergence,greeks,profiling}}.html` and `results/approach2/{args.hedging_dataset}/{{training,comparison,loss_histogram}}.html`.\",\n+              \"<!-- GENERATED_RESULTS_END -->\"]\n+    text = \"\\n\\n\".join(lines)\n+    path = ROOT/\"report.md\"\n+    report = path.read_text()\n+    start,end = \"<!-- GENERATED_RESULTS_START -->\",\"<!-- GENERATED_RESULTS_END -->\"\n+    if start in report:\n+        report = report[:report.index(start)]+text+report[report.index(end)+len(end):]\n+    else:\n+        report = report.replace(\"Pending numerical implementation, full execution, integration checks and Kimi's\\nfinal independent audit. No pricing, variance-reduction, convergence, speedup or\\nneural-performance claim is made at this stage.\",text)\n+    path.write_text(report)\n+    print(\"Generated factual report tables from full-size metrics\")\n+\n+\n+if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n+    main()\n*** End Patch"},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Success. I did not inspect or rely on the stale approach2 smoke metrics. Findings below concern current source; approach1 metrics are evidence from the existing run, not targets. All corrections are unexecuted proposals.\n\n### High priority\n\n1. **The CV convergence “RMSE slope” is reference-limited and must not be reported as estimator convergence.**  \n   **Code:** `code/approach1_pricing.py:166-175,188-225`.  \n   **Evidence:** `results/approach1/if_main/metrics.json:158-162,190-199,232-240,268-271`.  \n   The arithmetic-Asian reference has \\(SE_{\\rm ref}=0.20928\\). At \\(N=65536\\), the CV estimator’s own mean SE is only \\(0.02803\\), while its apparent RMSE remains \\(0.24707\\). Thus the reference error dominates, producing the fitted slope \\(-0.05484\\), not the estimator’s theoretical \\(-\\tfrac12\\) convergence. The docstring discloses the floor, but the metrics still publish an unqualified `slope_rmse_asian_cv`.  \n   **Correction:** mark this slope `reference_limited` and exclude it from pass/fail claims. Because naive, antithetic, and fixed-independent-pilot CV estimators are unbiased, estimate convergence using empirical standard deviation across independent repetitions, with bias against the large reference reported separately. Alternatively, use a rigorously justified reference-error correction with uncertainty; do not merely delete the unfavorable slope.\n\n2. **Approach2’s full table and paired bootstrap do not use identical neural P&L.**  \n   **Code:** `code/approach2_hedging.py:336-352,474-498,504-507,569-575`.  \n   The table computes deltas from float32 paths but evaluates P&L using NumPy float64 paths. `_neural_losses`, used for bootstrap, instead computes the entire P&L in float32 Torch. BS uses NumPy float64 throughout. Therefore paired bootstrap comparisons can differ from the displayed neural table through both path rounding and accumulation precision, especially in tail CVaR.  \n   **Correction:** convert the best policy to float64 for evaluation, use the same `S_test_np` values for every decision, and call the same NumPy float64 P&L implementation for both table and bootstrap losses. Add an equality test between table losses and bootstrap losses before resampling.\n\n3. **Production can silently price an entirely different calibration.**  \n   **Code:** `code/mc_common.py:46-61,87-101`; both entry points call it at `approach1_pricing.py:399` and `approach2_hedging.py:455`.  \n   Missing calibration returns `S0=100,r=0.03,sigma=0.20`; an existing partial JSON silently fills absent fields from those defaults. This can produce plausible but invalid official results. Unit tests can continue using explicit `Model()` independently.  \n   **Correction:** require the calibration file and every required key for production; validate finite values, positive spot/strike/barrier/volatility/maturity, and valid integer steps. Do not fall back silently.\n\n4. **Metrics serialization permits invalid standard JSON.**  \n   **Code:** `code/mc_common.py:111-135`.  \n   `json.dumps` defaults to `allow_nan=True`. NaN can arise from one-path standard errors (`mc_common.py:399-403`), zero reference variances, or regression degrees of freedom (`:465-479`), yielding non-standard `NaN` tokens and potentially hiding failed training.  \n   **Correction:** recursively reject non-finite values and serialize with `allow_nan=False`; record failures explicitly rather than emitting apparently successful metrics. Current approach1 metrics inspected are finite.\n\n### Medium priority\n\n5. **Convergence seeds create exact cross-repetition/cross-estimator dependence.**  \n   **Code:** `code/approach1_pricing.py:184-204`.  \n   Repetition \\(q\\) uses naive seed \\(s\\) and antithetic seed \\(s+1\\); repetition \\(q+1\\) increments `counter` and uses that same \\(s+1\\) for naive simulation. The antithetic run’s first \\(n/2\\) base-shock rows therefore recur in the next naive run. Seeds within each individual estimator remain distinct, so this does not establish marginal RMSE bias, but the runs are not jointly independent as the experiment implies.  \n   **Correction:** use explicitly disjoint `SeedSequence` children indexed by estimator, path count, and repetition; add a seed-stream disjointness test.\n\n6. **There are no paired pathwise-versus-FD uncertainty comparisons.**  \n   **Code:** `code/approach1_pricing.py:450-475`; `tests/test_numerical.py:147-155`.  \n   Pathwise Greeks use seed offset 4000 and FD Greeks 5000. The only paired differences are pathwise versus analytic vanilla values (`metrics.json:481-489`). Independent-seed absolute-tolerance tests do not provide the requested paired comparison.  \n   **Correction:** on one common \\(Z\\), form per-path\n   \\[\n   D_i=PW_i-\\frac{P_i(S^+)-P_i(S^-)}{2h},\n   \\]\n   and report \\(\\bar D\\), its paired SE, and a z-score for every bump and continuous payoff.\n\n7. **Training lacks persisted best checkpoints and numerical-failure guards.**  \n   **Code:** `code/approach2_hedging.py:245-306,531-537`.  \n   An in-memory `best_state` exists, but no weights or best epoch are saved. Loss/gradient/parameter finiteness is not checked before optimizer updates. `grad_norm` is only the last minibatch’s post-backward norm, not an epoch norm. NaN validation can also prevent any best state from being established.  \n   **Correction:** check loss, gradients, and parameters before each update; fail or record a defined failed run. Save the best state per cost with best epoch, validation metric, and checkpoint hash.\n\n8. **Official/smoke runs can overwrite one another without an acceptance guard.**  \n   **Code:** `code/approach2_hedging.py:433-449,452-545`.  \n   Although the default is correctly \\(2^{17}\\), arbitrary smaller `--n-train` values are accepted and written through the same output path without a smoke/full status. The current stale smoke output illustrates this operational risk; it is not evidence against the forthcoming full run.  \n   **Correction:** require \\(n_{\\rm train}\\ge131072\\) for official runs, or require an explicit `--smoke` mode writing to a separate path that `compare.py` excludes.\n\n9. **Cost sensitivity and bootstrap evidence omit important uncertainty/metadata.**  \n   **Code:** `code/approach2_hedging.py:355-370,481-484,538-544`.  \n   Each cost uses a different training seed, confounding cost effects with initialization/minibatch randomness. Paired path bootstrap measures neither retraining uncertainty nor this seed variation. Additionally, `n_boot`, bootstrap seeds, and the observed CVaR difference are absent; only the bootstrap-mean difference and CI are saved.  \n   **Correction:** use common initialization/minibatch seeds for the primary cost sensitivity and preferably repeat training across seeds. Begin Patch\n*** Update File: AUDIT.md\n@@\n independent data test. This is **M1-only** evidence, not complete Option A/B reproduction.\n+\n+## Integrated numerical audit (Kimi, same child session)\n+\n+Kimi identified reference-limited CV convergence, overlapping convergence seeds,\n+missing PW–FD paired uncertainty, silent calibration defaults and permissive NaN\n+serialization. The lead independently confirmed these and delegated the Option A/\n+shared-module repairs to DeepSeek. Original results are retained as exploratory\n+evidence, not overwritten as if the first convergence experiment had passed.\n+\n+For Option B, Kimi confirmed table/bootstrap precision mismatch and absent saved\n+checkpoints/gradient guards. Lead repairs now use a float64 copy of each trained\n+policy and identical float64 paths/NumPy P&L for both tables and bootstrap, with an\n+explicit equality check. Training remains float32. Checkpoints and histories are\n+persisted; nonfinite loss/gradient and CVaR inputs fail explicitly; best epoch is\n+recorded. Official entry points now reject fewer than 131072 training paths.\n+Bootstrap output includes the observed difference, resample count and seed.\n+\n+Independent lead tests verify literal irregular-interval P&L, NumPy/Torch agreement,\n+transaction cost sign, fractional CVaR against independently minimized RU objective,\n+future-path perturbation causality, autograd finite differences, and exact equality\n+of table/bootstrap evaluation metrics. Six integration/data tests passed after the\n+repairs. Numerical full-run acceptance remains pending.\n+\n+**Accepted uncertainty limitation:** different cost-specific model initialization\n+seeds mean the cross-cost neural sensitivity does not isolate costs from training\n+randomness. This is **M1-only** evidence, not complete Option A/B reproduction.\n+\n+## Integrated numerical audit (Kimi, same child session)\n+\n+Kimi identified reference-limited CV convergence, overlapping convergence seeds,\n+missing PW–FD paired uncertainty, silent calibration defaults and permissive NaN\n+serialization. The lead independently confirmed these and delegated the Option A/\n+shared-module repairs to DeepSeek. Original results are retained as exploratory\n+evidence, not overwritten as if the first convergence experiment had passed.\n+\n+For Option B, Kimi confirmed table/bootstrap precision mismatch and absent saved\n+checkpoints/gradient guards. Lead repairs now use a float64 copy of each trained\n+policy and identical float64 paths/NumPy P&L for both tables and bootstrap, with an\n+explicit equality check. Training remains float32. Checkpoints and histories are\n+persisted; nonfinite loss/gradient and CVaR inputs fail explicitly; best epoch is\n+recorded. Official entry points now reject fewer than 131072 training paths.\n+Bootstrap output includes the observed difference, resample count and seed.\n+\n+Independent lead tests verify literal irregular-interval P&L, NumPy/Torch agreement,\n+transaction cost sign, fractional CVaR against independently minimized RU objective,\n+future-path perturbation causality, autograd finite differences, and exact equality\n+of table/bootstrap evaluation metrics. Six integration/data tests passed after the\n+repairs. Numerical full-run acceptance remains pending.\n+\n+**Accepted uncertainty limitation:** different cost-specific model initialization\n+seeds mean the cross-cost neural sensitivity does not isolate costs from training\n+randomness. Paired-path intervals are conditional on fitted policies, not retraining\n+uncertainty. No claim of a causal cost effect or universal neural superiority is made.\n+\n+An already-running exploratory 50-epoch job predates these repairs. The separate\n+full-size integrated run uses dataset label `if_main_verified`, so its results cannot\n+be confused with the old smoke/full outputs. Here is the factual status.\n\n## Files I own & edited (this session)\n`code/mc_common.py`, `code/approach1_pricing.py`, `tests/test_numerical.py`. **`code/approach2_hedging.py` was NOT edited** (lead-owned).\n\n## 1. Archive\nOriginal Option A outputs preserved at `results/archive/initial_option_a/` (metrics.json + 3 figures, copied before rerun).\n\n## 2. Repairs completed (each verified)\n\n1. **`load_model` strict + validation** — now raises `FileNotFoundError` (absent file), `KeyError` (missing keys), `ValueError` (invalid params). Added `validate_model()` (rejects S0/K/B≤0, sigma≤0, T≤0, non-finite r/mu, non-positive-integer steps). `write_metrics` uses `json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False)`; `_to_jsonable` fixed to call `tolist()` for ndarrays **before** any `item()`, and stringifies non-str dict keys.\n2. **Reference replaced** — `asian_reference` → `asian_cv_reference`: independent pilot β (`estimate_control_beta`) + chunked **antithetic** production using exact discrete geometric expectation, **distinct chunk seeds** (no RNG reuse); returns `n_simulated_paths, n, beta, n_pilot, se`. Default `--ref-paths 2^22` → **ref SE 0.00350, 8.0× below the smallest CV SE (0.02811)**. Floor documented, not forced.\n3. **Convergence** — `spawn_seed_grid` uses `numpy.random.SeedSequence` to spawn disjoint streams by (n, rep, method); repeated price arrays stored in `history.convergence_prices`; slopes now reported with **bootstrap CIs** (`--n-boot-slope 500`) plus OLS SE. from: /Users/young/Desktop/advanced-programming-2026-q2/.cache/reproduction-4c6c8aff-20261104T090738342929/AGENTS.md\n# Advanced Programming 2026 — Question 2 Agent Contract\n\n## 1. Scope and ownership\n\nImplement **Question 2: Monte Carlo pricing and hedging on Chinese futures** in full, including **both Option A and Option B**, using the instructor's assignment (`assignment.md`) as the authoritative specification. Do not implement other questions in this repository unless explicitly requested.\n\nThe agent may implement code, acquire data, run experiments, create figures, draft technical explanations, and manage Git. **The student group remains responsible for mathematical decisions, verification of results, and the final English report.** Distinguish verified output from assumptions, drafts, and unresolved issues. Never fabricate empirical results, test results, commit history, or agent session logs.\n\n**Before beginning:** Read this file and `assignment.md` completely. If `assignment.md` is missing, request the original assignment before implementing specification-dependent work. Check existing files, Git history, available agents, and permissions. Preserve any existing work.\n\n## 2. Environment and reproducibility\n\n- **Python:** 3.13 (use `uv`); maintain `pyproject.toml` and a committed `uv.lock` with pinned dependency versions.\n- **Libraries:** NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn where useful, PyTorch (`torch`), Plotly, Rich, AKShare, and test/profiling tools as needed.\n- **Caches and artifacts:** All writes, caches, temporary files, and model checkpoints must remain **within the repository root**. Set `UV_CACHE_DIR=.cache/uv` and configure other tools similarly. Ignore `.venv/`, `.cache/`, `__pycache__/`, `results/`, regenerable `data/raw/`, credentials, and `*.ipynb` in `.gitignore`.\n- **Randomness:** Global CLI seed defaults to `42`, with `--seed` override. Seed each stochastic component, use independent train/validation/test seeds, and disclose nondeterminism.\n- **Scripts:** Each approach script must support `argparse` and run as a linear pipeline: load → verify → simulate/fit → evaluate → write outputs. Print readable output using Rich.\n- **Metrics:** Write `results/approachN/<dataset>/metrics.json` with at least `{\"params\": {...}, \"metrics\": {...}, \"fit_seconds\": ..., \"history\": {...}}`. Ensure JSON values are valid and documented.\n- **Figures:** Plotly standalone HTML with `include_plotlyjs=True`. `code/compare.py` must aggregate approach results, print ranked/comparison tables, and generate `results/comparison.html`.\n- **Offline grading:** Every remote data source must have a reproducible retrieval script and a committed usable offline snapshot per the assignment's size policy; record provenance, retrieval date, schema, and SHA-256 hashes in `data/metadata.json`. A fresh clone must be able to run without remote data access.\n\n### Target run commands\n\nMake the following commands work from the repository root after implementation; document any required flags and an offline option in `README.md` (maximum 10 lines):\n\n```bash\nexport UV_CACHE_DIR=.cache/uv\nuv sync --frozen\nuv run python data/fetch.py --help\nuv run python code/approach1_pricing.py --seed 42\nuv run python code/approach2_hedging.py --seed 42\nuv run python code/compare.py\n```\n\nThe fetch script must document the real-data retrieval command and also support reproduction from an existing offline snapshot. Do not treat `--help` as a data-fetch test.\n\n## 3. Data and mathematical specification\n\n- Obtain **at least five years of daily Chinese futures prices**, preferably CSI 300 futures (`IF`), using authorized FastboxData or available AKShare interfaces. Retrieve underlying index history as relevant and SHIBOR term structure data for discounting.\n- Document the contract series used, continuous-contract rolls, any artificial jumps, missing observations, data transformations, and the estimation window.\n- Estimate historical drift and annualized volatility from documented return calculations. Keep historical drift estimation separate from risk-neutral pricing.\n- Implement the **assignment-prescribed** exact GBM simulation under the risk-neutral measure:\n\n  \\[\n  S_{t_{i+1}}=S_{t_i}\\exp\\!\\left[(r-\\tfrac12\\sigma^2)\\Delta t+\\sigma\\sqrt{\\Delta t}\\,Z_i\\right],\n  \\qquad Z_i\\overset{iid}{\\sim}N(0,1).\n  \\]\n\n- Use at least **252 simulation steps per year**, with stated monitoring and averaging conventions.\n- **Model distinction:** A futures *price* under standard risk-neutral assumptions is typically modeled with zero drift (Black-76 convention), while the assignment explicitly requests a GBM with drift `r`. Implement the required assignment model for its Black–Scholes validation, but explicitly distinguish it from a futures-price model; never silently conflate the two. If a secondary Black-76 check is feasible, label it separately.\n- Price **all three required payoffs using both NumPy and PyTorch MC engines**:\n  1. Arithmetic Asian call: `max(mean(S[t_1],...,S[t_m]) - K, 0)`.\n  2. Discretely monitored up-and-out call: `max(S_T - K, 0) * 1{max(S[t_1],...,S[t_m]) < B}` (state whether the initial point is monitored).\n  3. Digital call: `1{S_T > K}`.\n- Include a European vanilla call to validate simulation against Black–Scholes: report `z = (MC_price - BS_price) / MC_standard_error` and check `|z| <= 3`. If a validation fails, investigate; do not conceal it.\n\n## 4. Option A — Monte Carlo engine, Greeks, and performance\n\nImplement and evaluate **all** required components:\n\n1. **Naive MC**, **antithetic variates** `(Z,-Z)`, and **geometric-Asian control variate**. Use the correct geometric-Asian expectation for the same **discrete observation schedule**, estimate the control coefficient consistently, and report variance-reduction ratios with valid uncertainty estimates. The indicative target is variance reduction factor ≥ 5 for Asian payoff; never force or fabricate a pass.\n2. **Delta and vega** using (i) valid pathwise estimators and (ii) central finite differences with bump sizes `h in {0.1, 0.01, 0.001} * S0` as required by the assignment (state how vega bumps are scaled). Use common random numbers in finite differences. Explain why naive pathwise differentiation can fail for discontinuous digital and barrier payoffs. Check analytical benchmarks where available and compare within reported standard errors.\n3. **Convergence experiments:** repeated independent runs across multiple path counts; RMSE versus N in log–log coordinates for all estimators, and fitted slope compared with theoretical `-1/2`. Report fitted values and uncertainty, not assumed success.\n4. **Computational profiling:** naive Python loops versus vectorized NumPy at the same workload, repeated `timeit` measurements, and an actual hot-loop profile using `line_profiler` or equivalent. Report runtime and speedup without hiding memory costs.\n\n## 5. Option B — Deep hedging in PyTorch\n\n1. Use the same simulation and payoff conventions as above; independently check agreement of NumPy and PyTorch prices within statistical error.\n2. Implement a trading policy `Delta_theta(t) = f_theta(S_t / S_0, t)` with an MLP having **at most three hidden layers**. Ensure decisions use only information available at time `t`.\n3. Implement the **assignment-specified** terminal hedging P&L with proportional costs:\n\n   \\[\n   V_T=\\sum_t e^{r(T-t)}\\Delta_t(S_{t+\\Delta t}-S_t)\n       -\\kappa\\sum_t|\\Delta_t-\\Delta_{t-1}|S_t-H(S).\n   \\]\n\n   Specify time indices, initial holding, premium convention, cost accumulation convention, and terminal closeout treatment. Apply the **same convention** to neural and baseline policies. If the assignment's stated cash-flow timing is simplified, explain rather than silently alter it.\n4. Define `L = -V_T` and minimize empirical **CVaR at alpha = 0.95**. A suitable training objective is the Rockafellar–Uryasev form `min_{theta, eta} eta + (1/(1-alpha)) mean(relu(L_theta - eta))`. Verify quantile/CVaR evaluation independently from training loss.\n5. Use **at least `2^17 = 131072` simulated training paths**. Use minibatches, independent validation/test paths and seeds, monitored training history, and defensible early stopping.\n6. Compare with **Black–Scholes delta hedging** at rebalancing intervals **1, 5, and 21 trading days** and transaction costs **0, 10, and 50 basis points** (`0`, `0.001`, `0.005`). Report **CVaR(95%)**, **P&L variance**, and **expected P&L** for each required combination; additionally report trading turnover and average cost if feasible.\n7. Use the European vanilla call for the cleanest analytic BS-delta benchmark. If deep hedging other payoffs, use a payoff-consistent delta benchmark or clearly label a proxy. Do not compare option strategies on mismatched payoffs, paths, premiums, or accounting conventions.\n8. Evaluate on held-out paths; do not claim neural outperformance unless supported by out-of-sample results. A risk-neutral simulator's CVaR is a model-implied loss measure, not automatically a physical-measure market-risk result.\n\n## 6. Required repository structure\n\n```text\nrepo/\n  AGENTS.md\n  .gitignore\n  README.md\n  assignment.md              # source specification, if permitted to include\n  pyproject.toml\n  uv.lock\n  data/\n    fetch.py\n    raw/                     # gitignored when regenerable\n    clean/                   # committed offline fallback, subject to size rules\n    metadata.json\n  code/\n    approach1_pricing.py\n    approach2_hedging.py\n    compare.py\n  tests/\n  results/                   # reproducible outputs; normally gitignored\n  report.md\n  SESSION.md\n```\n\nMaintain additional modules only when useful; required entry points and outputs must remain discoverable. Do not store secrets, account credentials, API keys, or tokens in the repository.\n\n## 7. Multi-agent orchestration: ChatGPT + DeepSeek + Kimi\n\n**Approved execution environment:** Use **OpenCode or an approved OpenCode-compatible terminal agent** for all assignment-producing sessions. ChatGPT/OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Kimi refer to **models/providers inside OpenCode**, not standalone apps used instead of OpenCode. Do **not** invoke Gemini or depend on Gemini credentials.\n\n### 7.1 Roles and file ownership\n\n**ChatGPT / OpenAI — lead agent (`chatgpt-lead`, primary)**\n- Own the mathematical specification, risk-neutral convention, payoff definitions, shared interfaces, parameters, and experiment protocol. Make and document methodological decisions for group review.\n- Coordinate the other agents, integrate and debug all implementations, manage Git commits and reproducibility, run cross-engine tests, and prepare the **draft** English report and statement of work.\n- Own `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `data/fetch.py`, `data/metadata.json`, `code/compare.py`, `tests/integration_*`, and `report.md`; coordinate rather than concurrently edit subagent-owned files.\n- Independently check numerical claims, especially exact GBM moments, European BS z-scores, payoff conventions, risk measures, train/test segregation, and whether experimental conclusions follow from actual results.\n\n**DeepSeek — numerical engineering (`deepseek-numerical`, subagent)**\n- Primary coding responsibility for `code/approach1_pricing.py` and `code/approach2_hedging.py` and associated isolated numerical helper modules/tests.\n- Implement reproducible NumPy/PyTorch engines, Asian/barrier/digital payoffs, antithetic and geometric-Asian control variates, Greeks, RMSE experiments, profiling, MLP, P&L, CVaR training, and benchmark sweeps.\n- Produce runnable code and actual diagnostic output, numerical timings, memory/use-of-seed disclosures. Explain unstable gradients, failed training, and computational bottlenecks; never assert benchmarks passed without evidence.\n- Before integration, send the lead explicit contracts for function signatures, units, file paths, metric keys, seeds, and required runtime/dependencies.\n\n**Kimi — independent long-context audit (`kimi-review`, read-only subagent)**\n- Review `assignment.md`, `AGENTS.md`, source files, tests, metrics, figures, report and Git milestones **together** for cross-file consistency and coverage. Use Kimi as an independent reviewer, not as an authority whose assertions substitute for test results.\n- Audit derivations and numerical edge cases independently: GBM drift versus futures/Black-76 conventions; exact discrete geometric-Asian expectation; antithetic sampling units; pathwise Greek validity; finite-difference common random numbers; CVaR tail orientation; option premium and transaction cost timing; train/test leakage; 3x3 BS hedge benchmarks; data provenance; reproducibility.\n- Provide a prioritized issue list with precise file/line references, why each issue matters, and a reproducible test or correction proposal. **Do not edit implementation files or silently fix code.** The lead reviews findings and delegates confirmed fixes to DeepSeek or integrates them directly.\n- During final acceptance, compare every material report claim with actual generated metrics/figures and verify no required deliverable is missing.\n\n### 7.2 Dispatch protocol\n\n1. The ChatGPT lead inspects `opencode agent list`, `opencode models`, available credentials, the actual repository and Git history. Model/agent IDs are installation-specific; **do not invent a provider/model identifier**. If a required provider is not available, mark it BLOCKED and report it rather than pretending to use it.\n2. The lead publishes a compact shared interface and experiment plan: model interpretation, parameters, CLI, output schema, seeds, fixed payoffs, timing and accounting conventions. Then delegates independent work.\n3. DeepSeek implements the numerical modules; ChatGPT simultaneously owns infrastructure/data retrieval and tests **in separate files**. Kimi can review the specification immediately; after coding, it reviews the integrated snapshot without editing.\n4. ChatGPT runs all executable tests and simulations, dispatches confirmed numerical defects to DeepSeek, checks Kimi's findings, and repeats testing until actual PASS or a clearly documented unresolved failure.\n5. Each milestone generates a separate real Git commit. Maintain authentic OpenCode parent and child-agent session evidence for the eventual `SESSION.md` export. Never fabricate subagent calls, commits, benchmark numbers, or logs.\n6. If a subagent cannot run within OpenCode, disclose the specific blocker and any approved substitution. Do not silently switch to standalone apps that violate the assignment's terminal-agent rule.\n\n### 7.3 Independent verification checklist\n\nRun automated and numerical checks for: GBM moments; BS MC z-score; payoff boundary cases; no barrier-overshoot counting error; discrete geometric-Asian expectation; covariance and antithetic standard errors; pathwise/finite-difference Greeks; convergence; NumPy/PyTorch agreement; CVaR upper-tail orientation; transaction cost sign/timing; absence of foresight; independence of train/test paths; complete benchmark coverage; offline reproduction.\n\nKimi's independent review must contain specific findings supported by reproducible evidence. ChatGPT must independently adjudicate those findings and ensure confirmed defects are repaired and the affected experiments rerun. Preserve failures and explain unresolved limitations.\n\n## 8. Git, permissions, and session integrity\n\n- **`AGENTS.md` must exist and have been committed before the first coding-agent session**, as required by the assignment. Inspect the actual history; if this condition was not met, report the discrepancy truthfully. Never backdate or fabricate commits.\n- Preserve existing repository history. Commit after each meaningful milestone with prefixes such as `chore:`, `data:`, `feat:`, `test:`, `exp:`, and `report:`. Do not squash everything into a single commit.\n- Never write outside the repository root; never force-push, rewrite history, delete data, or perform other destructive/irreversible actions without explicit user approval recorded in the genuine transcript.\n- Keep a **complete authentic** terminal-agent session export in root `SESSION.md`, including prompts, agent responses, tool calls, and child-agent sessions as supported. Export from the actual terminal agent; redact credentials but **do not fabricate transcripts**. If the export is finalized after the live session ends, provide exact finalization instructions and verify it before final submission.\n- Create the final `submission` Git tag **only after** the repository, report, session export, and clean-clone reproduction have passed verification. If this repository is only one question of a shared group project, coordinate the tag at the group-repository level.\n\n## 9. Report and acceptance criteria\n\nPrepare a factual **English draft** of `report.md` covering mathematical specifications for every estimator/model, data and calibration windows, protocols, pricing and validation tables, variance reduction, Greeks, RMSE convergence, profiling, training, all hedging benchmarks, transaction-cost sensitivity, limitations, figure references, reproducibility, and a **statement of work** describing what agents did versus what the group decided. The group must review and finalize the report itself.\n\nDo not mark the work complete until:\n\n1. Five-year real-data coverage and metadata/offline fallback are verified.\n2. All three required option payoffs are priced in **both** engines, and analytical checks are reported.\n3. All Option A requirements, numerical tables, and figures have actually run.\n4. All Option B training/test and mandatory cost/frequency combinations have actually run.\n5. Independent verification findings and repairs are recorded.\n6. A clean-clone offline reproduction and comparison output are verified.\n7. The required deliverables (`AGENTS.md`, code, `report.md`, `SESSION.md`) and milestone Git history exist.\n8. No empirical result, test, subagent invocation, or session record is invented.\n\nProceed autonomously through safe, reversible implementation steps after initialization.
